newsitem.title: USA: Conn. budget talks hit snag over retirement--paper.
newsitem.headline: Conn. budget talks hit snag over retirement--paper.

text.p: Connecticut's budget negotiations hit a snag over Gov John Rowland's plan to save $200 million with an early retirement program for state employees, the Hartford Courant said Monday.

Another contentious issue that remained unresolved was the governor's plan to save $50 million by privatizing the state's computer system. The paper said that the computer proposal was opposed by state employees and their union leaders as they fear it will lead to layoffs.

The negotiators worked through the weekend trying to thrash out the details of the $20.8 billion budget but by early Sunday evening Democratic leaders still had failed to produce crucial language on the early retirement program, the paper said.
While top Democrats and the state employee unions have agreed to a no-layoff provision for two years, the governor has not included the no-layoff provision in his plan.

The Democrats and Republicans agree that the the amount of money saved with the early retirement plan is linked to the size of tax cuts, a top priority for the governor. If the plan saves $120 million, for example, then lawmakers would need to cut $80 million in other programs or reduce the size of the tax cut to balance the two-year tax reduction, the paper said.
About 8,500 state employees would be eligible for the package, and Rowland's budget office forecast about one-third would take the package.

Rowland recommended spending $37 million over two years for a variety of programs to improve education, as well as $445 million of tax cuts that include cutting the state income tax by $365 million and reducing the state's gasoline tax by five cents per gallon on July 1.

Democrats have responded by saying they want to cut property taxes instead of income taxes, and lower the gasoline tax by six cents per gallon on July 1. At 39 cents per gallon, state gasoline taxes are the higest in the nation, the paper said.
